**SECTION 2: RESEARCH & THEORETICAL JUSTIFICATION**  
**Why Establish a Whole-School Vaping Initiative Now?**  
Adolescent e-cigarette use (vaping) represents one of the most rapidly escalating public health concerns across Australian secondary schools ([**Cancer Council Victoria, 2023**](https://www.cancervic.org.au/research/our-research/centre-for-behavioural-research-in-cancer/major-topics-projects/tobacco/victorian-secondary-student-smoking-attitudes-and-behaviours.html)). Grounded in empirical data and social-ecological theory, establishing a structured, whole-school health intervention is an urgent educational priority for three key reasons:

**1\. Epidemiological Urgency & Commercial Determinants**  
Recent national and Victorian health data indicate that **over 30% of Australian secondary students aged 14–17 have tried vaping**, with current regular usage expanding dramatically over the past four years ([**AIHW, 2024**](https://www.aihw.gov.au/reports/illicit-use-of-drugs/national-drug-strategy-household-survey-2022-2023/contents/summary); [**Cancer Council Victoria, 2023**](https://www.cancervic.org.au/research/our-research/centre-for-behavioural-research-in-cancer/major-topics-projects/tobacco/victorian-secondary-student-smoking-attitudes-and-behaviours.html)). Vaping is driven by aggressive **commercial determinants of health**—specifically deceptive flavourings (e.g., fruit/candy flavours), covert social media algorithms, and high-dose disposable nicotine delivery systems designed to create rapid youth dependency (Gardner et al., 2025).

**2\. The Failure of Punitive Surveillance & Misperceived Peer Norms**  
When schools respond to vaping through reactive, zero-tolerance measures—such as vape detection hardware, bathroom closures, or suspensions—they trigger student alienation and secretiveness without reducing nicotine dependency (Lockett et al., 2024). Suspensions disproportionately harm disadvantaged students by severing school connectedness. Furthermore, unaddressed peer environments foster **misperceived social norms**, causing teenagers to wildly overestimate how many of their peers vape, which increases social pressure to experiment (Asdigian et al., 2023).

**3\. Theoretical Foundation: Social-Ecological & Self-Efficacy Models**  
According to [Bronfenbrenner’s (1979) **Ecological Systems Theory**](https://www.simplypsychology.org/bronfenbrenner.html) and [Bandura's (1977) **Self-Efficacy Theory**](https://www.simplypsychology.org/self-efficacy.html), health behaviours cannot be changed in isolation. Effective health promotion requires aligning the student's microsystem (classroom HPE refusal mastery), mesosystem (peer-led school culture & parent partnerships), and exosystem (clinical nurse & Headspace pathways). By operationalising [HIWS Strategy 5 (*Fostering Self-Efficacy*)](https://www.google.com/search?q=https://www.education.vic.gov.au/school/teachers/classrooms/Pages/approaches-hiws.aspx) alongside [**Hart’s (1992) Ladder of Youth Participation**](https://www.yacvic.org.au/yerp/youth-participation-getting-started/youth-participation-models/) and [**Mitra’s (2008) Student Voice Framework**](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/291766912_Amplifying_Student_Voice), schools can move beyond tokenistic consultation to build genuine student refusal mastery, youth agency, and a positive school climate.

**SECTION 4: ULTIMATE AIM & CORE PHILOSOPHY**

**ULTIMATE PROJECT AIM**

Empower Victorian secondary students with critical health literacy and refusal assertiveness, while establishing student-led peer leadership and non-punitive clinical care pathways to replace exclusionary school discipline.         

**Core Pedagogical Pillars:**

* **Whole-School Multi-Tiered System of Support (MTSS):** Structuring health interventions across Tier 1 Universal Education (Years 7–8), Tier 2 Targeted Peer Leadership (Years 9–10), and Tier 3 Intensive Clinical Care (Years 11–12 & High Dependency).  
* **Authentic Student Voice & Co-Design:** Operationalising Hart’s (1992) Ladder of Youth Participation and Mitra’s (2008) Student Voice framework by moving from top-down adult directives ("doing to") to student co-produced peer campaigns ("doing with").  
* **High Impact Wellbeing Strategies (HIWS):** Explicitly building student refusal self-efficacy (Bandura, 1977\) and positive school climate under Victorian Department of Education standards (2021).  
* **Ecological & Cultural Family Partnerships:** Engaging Culturally and Linguistically Diverse (CALD) families through two-way health communication and multilingual resources (Bronfenbrenner, 1979).

**\[SECTION 1: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY & PROGRAM PHILOSOPHY\]**  
**Transforming Adolescent Health at Aurevian College**  
**Project Unclouded** is an evidence-informed, whole-school health promotion initiative designed specifically for the unique socio-demographic profile of Aurevian College in Melton South. Adolescent e-cigarette use (vaping) represents a complex, multi-faceted public health concern in Victoria, driven by commercial determinants of health, deceptive marketing, and misperceived peer social norms ([Cancer Council Victoria, 2023](https://www.cancervic.org.au/research/our-research/centre-for-behavioural-research-in-cancer/major-topics-projects/tobacco/victorian-secondary-student-smoking-attitudes-and-behaviours.html); [Victorian Department of Health \[VDH\], 2023](https://www.health.vic.gov.au/victorian-public-health-and-wellbeing-plan-2023-27)).

Rather than relying on isolated classroom interventions or punitive zero-tolerance surveillance, **Project Unclouded** operationalises a whole-school system of support. Aligned with the [*Framework for Improving Student Outcomes 2.0*](https://www2.education.vic.gov.au/pal/fiso/policy) (FISO 2.0; Department of Education, 2024), the [*High Impact Wellbeing Strategies*](https://www.education.vic.gov.au/Documents/school/teachers/teachingresources/practice/High-Impact-Wellbeing-Strategies-Resource2023.pdf) (HIWS; Department of Education, 2021), and the [*Victorian Healthy Places Framework for Schools*](https://healthyplaces.health.vic.gov.au/en/schools/healthy-places-framework-for-schools) (Healthy Places Healthy Futures, n.d.), this website equips school leaders, educators, and health personnel with a plug-and-play framework to:

1. **Deconstruct Commercial Determinants:** Build universal health literacy and refusal assertiveness among Year 7–8 students through evidence-backed curriculum units (Gardner et al., 2025).  
     
2. **Elevate Genuine Student Voice:** Train Year 9–10 "Wellbeing Champions" to co-design peer messaging and run the annual *Unclouded Peer Festival* under adult developmental safety monitoring (Asdigian et al., 2023; Lockett et al., 2024).  
     
3. **Bridge Home and School:** Mobilise Aurevian's rich Culturally and Linguistically Diverse (CALD) community through multilingual, two-way family engagement.  
     
4. **Establish Non-Punitive Health Pathways:** Divert students exhibiting nicotine dependency away from exclusionary suspensions and into confidential, stepped-care clinical support (Thomas et al., 2025).

**Why Local Context Matters for Health Promotion:**

* **Addressing Commercial Targeting:** Youth in lower socio-economic corridors face heightened exposure to retail vaping displays and targeted digital marketing.  
    
* **Culturally Sensitive Health Literacy:** With 53% of families coming from CALD backgrounds, standard English health notifications often fail to engage parents. Project Unclouded embeds bilingual parent flyers and works alongside Aurevian's CALD Liaison Officer to build genuine two-way health partnerships.  
    
* **Protecting School Connectedness:** Disadvantaged students subjected to exclusionary discipline (suspensions) face disproportionate risks of disengagement, academic failure, and escalation into criminal justice pathways. Replacing zero-tolerance exclusions with internal health support preserves vital access to education.

**Overview of Whole-School Tiers**  
**Tier 1: Universal Prevention (Whole School & Years 7–8)**

* **HPE Curriculum Integration:** 4-hour *OurFutures* vaping unit delivered in Year 7–8 HPE classes, focusing on social norm correction, refusal mastery, and commercial marketing literacy (Gardner et al., 2025).  
    
* **Whole-School Climate:** Annual *Unclouded Peer Festival*, voluntary perimeter signage under the *Tobacco Act 1987*, and positive health messaging across school communications.


**Tier 2: Targeted Peer Leadership & Early Intervention (Years 9–10 & At-Risk Youth)**

* **Wellbeing Champions:** 15 student leaders co-designing anti-vaping campaigns and running festival activity booths, empowering student agency while applying adult safety reviews to prevent norm inflation (Asdigian et al., 2023; Hunter, 2023).  
    
* **Early Support Check-Ins:** Confidential, voluntary consultations with the Secondary School Nurse or Mental Health Practitioner for students showing early vaping experimentation.


**Tier 3: Intensive Clinical Pathways (Years 11–12 & High Nicotine Dependency)**

* **Confidential Individual Support Plans:** Tailored Nicotine Cessation Plans developed collaboratively by the Secondary School Nurse, Mental Health Practitioner, and student.  
    
* **External Clinical Referrals:** Stepped-care escalation to *headspace Melton*, *Quitline Victoria*, or general practitioners for high-dependency cases, explicitly prohibiting suspension as a default response (Department of Education, 2024; Thomas et al., 2025).


**\[SECTION 4: EXPECTED SYSTEMIC IMPACT & EVALUATION\]**  
**Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)**  
Project Unclouded will evaluate success across quantitative health metrics and qualitative systemic indicators:

* **25% Increase in Nurse Self-Referrals:** Demonstrating elevated health literacy and trust in non-punitive, confidential support within 12 months.  
    
* **50% Reduction in Vape-Related Suspensions:** Successfully redirecting students from exclusionary discipline into Tier 2 and Tier 3 Individual Support Plans.  
    
* **Statistically Significant Norm Correction:** Statistically significant reduction in past-30-day e-cigarette use and susceptibility scores on post-intervention student surveys.  
    
* **High Implementation Fidelity:** Achieving sustained compliance across all six domains of the *Victorian Healthy Places Framework for Schools*.

**\[SECTION 1 OVERVIEW & PEDAGOGICAL PHILOSOPHY\]**  
   
**Why Initiative-Informed Planning Matters**  
Traditional school-based health education often relies on isolated, top-down instructional units or reactive zero-tolerance discipline. However, evidence demonstrates that fragmented interventions fail to alter complex health behaviours such as adolescent e-cigarette use (vaping) because they ignore the broader social, cultural, and environmental determinants of health (Victorian Department of Health \[VDH\], 2023; World Health Organisation \[WHO\], 2021).  
   
To achieve sustained, positive health and educational outcomes, health promotion must be grounded in systemic, evidence-based educational initiatives. Aligned with the *Framework for Improving Student Outcomes 2.0* (FISO 2.0; Department of Education, 2024\) and the *Victorian Healthy Places Framework for Schools* (Healthy Places Healthy Futures, n.d.), **Project Unclouded** integrates three foundational pillars:

1. **Student Voice, Agency, and Partnership:** Moving from passive instruction to genuine power-sharing and student-led co-design (Hunter, 2023).  
      
2. **High Impact Wellbeing Strategies (HIWS):** Operationalising Strategy 5 (*Fostering Student Self-Efficacy*) and Strategy 3 (*Creating Safe and Inclusive Environments*) to build emotional regulation, resilience, and refusal mastery (Department of Education, 2021).  
      
3. **Community & Family Partnerships:** Leveraging Bronfenbrenner’s ecological model and Indigenous Social and Emotional Wellbeing (SEWB) perspectives to create bi-directional engagement with Aurevian College's 53% Culturally and Linguistically Diverse (CALD) community and local health services.  
    

**\[INITIATIVE CARD 1: STUDENT VOICE, AGENCY & THE PARTICIPATION CONTINUUM\]**  
   
**INITIATIVE 1: STUDENT VOICE, AGENCY & POWER-SHARING**

| THEORETICAL & LITERATURE FOUNDATIONS | PROGRAM APPLICATION AT AUREVIAN COLLEGE |
| :---- | :---- |
| • Participation Continuum (Shifting from "doing to" → "doing with"). • Lockett et al. (2024): Youth preference for peer connection over surveillance. • Asdigian et al. (2023): Developmental scaffolding in peer messaging. | • Year 9–10 Wellbeing Champions (15 student leaders) co-designing peer festival stalls. • Adult Safety Review Protocol: Preventing accidental norm inflation (p \= .002) through guided developmental oversight. • Peer-to-Peer Health Advocacy. |

   
   
**![][image6]**  
**1\. Theoretical Rationale & Policy Context**  
Student voice is frequently misconstrued as simple consultation or tokenistic feedback collection. In contrast, Monash health education researcher Lisa Hunter (2023) conceptualises student voice along a **Participation Continuum**:

* **Low Agency (*Doing to*):** Coercion, educating, and informing. Students are passive recipients of adult directives.  
     
* **Medium Agency (*Doing for*):** Consulting and engaging. Adults collect student opinions but retain all decision-making authority.  
     
* **High Agency (*Doing with*):** Co-designing, collaborating, and co-producing. Students and educators share power, agency, and responsibility.  
   

When health initiatives operate at the "doing to" level—such as installing vape detectors or issuing punitive suspensions—they trigger student alienation, defiance, and secretiveness (Lockett et al., 2024). Adolescents strongly prefer health models grounded in peer connection, agency, and supportive relationships over adult surveillance (Lockett et al., 2024).

**PARTICIPATION CONTINUUM IN HEALTH PROMOTION**

| Low Agency ("Doing To") | → Medium Agency ("Doing For") | → High Agency ("Doing With") |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Punitive Suspensions & Vape Surveillance Devices | Student Surveys & Adult-Driven Health Campaigns | PROJECT UNCLOUDED: Student Co-Designed Peer Festival |

                
![][image7]  
   
**2\. Practical Application in Project Unclouded**  
Project Unclouded operationalises high-agency participation by establishing a cohort of 15 **Year 9–10 Wellbeing Champions**. Rather than consuming pre-packaged anti-vaping flyers, these student leaders undergo structured co-design workshops (Module 2, Hours 5–7) to author digital media assets and run interactive stalls during the *Unclouded Peer Festival*.

**Critical Nuance: Adult Safety Review Protocol**  
While empowering student voice is critical, unguided peer health messaging carries risks. Asdigian et al. (2023) demonstrated that unmonitored peer-led campaigns can accidentally cause **social norm inflation** (![][image8])—unintentionally exaggerating the perceived prevalence of vaping and making adolescents believe "everyone is doing it."  
   
To mitigate this risk, Project Unclouded embeds an **Adult Safety Review Protocol**. Health and Physical Education (HPE) teachers and the Secondary School Nurse act as developmental mentors, validating student-created content against Australian Institute of Health and Welfare (AIHW, 2024\) empirical prevalence data before public distribution.

**\[INITIATIVE CARD 2: HIGH IMPACT WELLBEING STRATEGIES & SELF-EFFICACY\]**  
   
**INITIATIVE 2: HIGH IMPACT WELLBEING STRATEGIES (HIWS)**

| THEORETICAL & LITERATURE FOUNDATIONS | PROGRAM APPLICATION AT AUREVIAN COLLEGE |
| :---- | :---- |
| • DET HIWS Strategy 5: Fostering Student Self-Efficacy & Agency. • DET HIWS Strategy 3: Safe, Inclusive, and Respectful Environments. • Bandura (1977): Self-Efficacy Theory as the foundation for behavioural change. | • Bandura’s 4 Sources of Self-Efficacy: 1\. Mastery: Refusal skill role-plays. 2\. Vicarious: Peer-led festival stalls. 3\. Social Persuasion: Nurse check-ins. 4\. Affective State: Reduced social anxiety. • Non-punitive, supportive school climate. |

   
**![][image9]**  
**1\. Theoretical Rationale & Policy Context**  
The Victorian Department of Education’s *High Impact Wellbeing Strategies* (HIWS; 2021\) provide a practical policy blueprint for integrating health and learning. Project Unclouded explicitly operationalises **HIWS Strategy 5: Foster Student Self-Efficacy** and **HIWS Strategy 3: Create Safe and Inclusive Environments**.  
   
Albert Bandura’s (1977) **Self-Efficacy Theory** posits that an individual's belief in their capability to execute specific behaviours dictates whether they will initiate and sustain health-promoting actions. In adolescent vaping prevention, self-efficacy is the critical psychological mechanism required for a student to resist social pressure, refuse e-cigarettes, and seek help for nicotine dependency (Gardner et al., 2025).

**2\. Practical Application: Operationalising Bandura’s 4 Sources of Self-Efficacy**  
Project Unclouded explicitly embeds Bandura's four sources of self-efficacy across its 10-hour activity sequence:

 **BANDURA'S (1977) FOUR SOURCES OF SELF-EFFICACY — PROGRAM INTEGRATION**

| SOURCE OF EFFICACY | PROJECT UNCLOUDED IMPLEMENTATION |
| :---- | :---- |
| 1\. Mastery Experiences (Performance Success) | Students practice social assertiveness and refusal scripts during Module 1 (Hour 3\) HPE scenario role-plays. |
| 2\. Vicarious Experiences (Peer Modelling) | Younger students observe Year 9–10 Wellbeing Champions modelling healthy choices and running festival booths. |
| 3\. Verbal / Social Persuasion (Encouragement) | Secondary School Nurses and peers reinforce positive social norms (e.g., "Over 84% of local teens choose not to vape"). |
| 4\. Emotional / Affective State Management | Creating a safe, non-punitive environment reduces peer anxiety and removes fear of suspension during help-seeking. |

   
   
**![][image10]**  
**\[INITIATIVE CARD 3: COMMUNITY & CALD FAMILY PARTNERSHIPS\]**  
   
**INITIATIVE 3: COMMUNITY & FAMILY PARTNERSHIPS**

| THEORETICAL & LITERATURE FOUNDATIONS | PROGRAM APPLICATION AT AUREVIAN COLLEGE |
| :---- | :---- |
| • Bronfenbrenner’s Ecological Systems Model (Microsystem to Macrosystem alignment). • Social & Emotional Wellbeing (SEWB) Model (Multidimensional, holistic health). • Bi-directional, two-way communication. | • Multi-Lingual Resources: East African & South Asian parent flyers (CALD Liaison). • External Clinical Pathways: Headspace Melton & Secondary School Nurse. • Community Showcase Evening (Hour 10). |

![][image11]  
   
**1\. Theoretical Rationale & Policy Context**  
Adolescent wellbeing cannot be isolated within classroom walls. Grounded in Bronfenbrenner’s **Ecological Systems Theory** (1979) and the Indigenous **Social and Emotional Wellbeing (SEWB)** framework (Gee et al., 2014), health promotion must engage the entire ecosystem surrounding the young person—connecting the individual to family, school, health services, and broader cultural communities.

                    **WHOLE-SCHOOL PARTNERSHIP ECOSYSTEM (BRONFENBRENNER, 1979\)**

| SYSTEM LEVEL | PARTNERSHIP ECOSYSTEM |
| :---- | :---- |
| MACROSYSTEM | Cultural Ideologies, Public Health Laws (Tobacco Act 1987\) |
| EXOSYSTEM | VDH Policy, Headspace Melton, Local Government Area (LGA) Data |
| MESOSYSTEM | Home-School Partnerships, CALD Community Networks, Nurse Pathways |
| MICROSYSTEM | Aurevian College Classroom, Family Unit, Peer Group |
| INDIVIDUAL STUDENT | Health Literacy, Self-Efficacy, Agency |

   
![][image12]  
At Aurevian College, where **53% of students come from CALD backgrounds** (specifically East African, South Sudanese, and South Asian cohorts), traditional one-way English notifications (e.g., punitive letters sent home regarding vaping infractions) erode trust and fail to foster health literacy (ABS, 2022). Effective partnerships require **bi-directional communication**—valuing cultural perspectives, addressing commercial determinants at home, and building a shared community identity around youth safety.

**2\. Practical Application in Project Unclouded**

* **Bi-Lingual Family Health Literacy:** Working alongside Aurevian’s CALD Liaison Officer, key health promotion materials, refusal strategies, and nicotine dependency information are translated into priority community languages (Swahili, Arabic, Dinka, Punjabi, Hindi).  
     
* **Integrated Clinical Pathways:** Establishing formal, non-punitive referral pathways with **headspace Melton** and the **Secondary School Nursing Program**. Students exhibiting severe nicotine dependency are offered voluntary, confidential cessation support rather than exclusionary discipline (Thomas et al., 2025).  
     
* **Multi-Lingual Family Showcase (Hour 10):** The project culminates in an evening showcase where CALD families attend student-led stalls, breaking down language barriers and reinforcing health messaging at home.

**\[SECTION 2: DETAILED 10-HOUR ACTIVITY SEQUENCE\]**  
**MODULE 1: Universal Health Literacy & Social Norm Correction (4 Hours)**

* **Delivery Setting:** Year 7 & 8 Health and Physical Education (HPE) Core Classes  
    
* **Target Cohort:** All Year 7–8 Students (Tier 1 Universal)


**HOUR 1: DECONSTRUCTING COMMERCIAL DETERMINANTS & VAPING MARKETING HACKS**

| COMPONENT | DETAILS |
| :---- | :---- |
| Activity Focus | Critical media analysis of e-cigarette branding, flavourings, and covert social media marketing targeting adolescents (Gardner et al., 2025). |
| Key Student Tasks | Students analyse sample vape packaging and social media ad mock-ups, identifying tactics used by manufacturers to create youth nicotine addiction. |
| Initiatives Embedded | High Impact Wellbeing Strategies (HIWS Strategy 3: Safe, Critical Classroom Environments). |
| Evidence of Learning | Completed "Commercial Tactics Deconstruction Worksheet" and group map of industry marketing strategies. |

**HOUR 2: BUSTING VAPING NORMS: PERCEPTION VS. REALITY DATA**

| COMPONENT | DETAILS |
| :---- | :---- |
| Activity Focus | Correcting perceived social norms regarding peer vaping prevalence to reduce social pressure and norm exaggeration (AIHW, 2024; Asdigian et al., 2023). |
| Key Student Tasks | Students participate in an interactive poll comparing their guessed peer vaping rates against official AIHW and Victorian secondary school survey data (showing over 84% of Victorian teens do not vape regularly). |
| Initiatives Embedded | HIWS Strategy 5 (Building Cognitive Self-Efficacy); Student Voice (analysing self-generated cohort survey data). |
| Evidence of Learning | Norm Correction Infographic highlighting true local non-vaping data. |

**HOUR 3: REFUSAL MASTERY & SOCIAL ASSERTIVENESS ROLEPLAYS**

| COMPONENT | DETAILS |
| :---- | :---- |
| Activity Focus | Behavioural skill-building applying Bandura’s (1977) Performance Mastery source of self-efficacy in social pressure scenarios. |
| Key Student Tasks | Students practice structured refusal scripts ("CLEAR" model: Calm, Logical, Emphatic, Alternative offer, Redirect) in small-group peer scenarios. |
| Initiatives Embedded | HIWS Strategy 5 (Mastery Experiences); Peer Collaboration.Refusal Script Roleplay Assessment Rubric completed via peer feedback logs. |
| Evidence of Learning | Peer-evaluated roleplay performances and refusal reflection journal. |

**HOUR 4: DIGITAL HEALTH LITERACY & OURFUTURES INTERACTIVE MODULES**

| COMPONENT | DETAILS |
| :---- | :---- |
| Activity Focus | Evidence-based digital learning using adapted modules from the validated *OurFutures* e-health vaping prevention program (Gardner et al., 2025). |
| Key Student Tasks | Students complete interactive online comic storylines navigating decisions around vaping, nicotine dependence, and support-seeking options. |
| Initiatives Embedded | Independent Digital Literacy; Confidential Help-Seeking Awareness. |
| Evidence of Learning | OurFutures Module Completion Certificate and self-reflection log. |

**\[SECTION 3: CULMINATING EVENT DEEP-DIVE\]**  
**Detailed Overview: The Unclouded Peer Festival**  
The culmination of Project Unclouded is not a traditional written exam or teacher presentation, but a **vibrant, student-owned health festival**. This approach honours Hart’s (1992) Ladder of Youth Participation and Mitra’s (2008) Student Voice Framework by positioning students as active health advocates rather than passive consumers of information.

**UNCLOUDED PEER FESTIVAL MAP & STALL LAYOUT**

| STALL 1: MYTH-BUSTING SPIN WHEEL | STALL 2: REFUSAL CHALLENGE ZONE | STALL 3: SMOOTHIE BIKE ENERGY STATION |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Peer Norm Correction Data (AIHW Prevalence Stats) | Live Refusal Roleplays & Assertiveness Games | Healthy Alternatives & Stress Management |

| STALL 4: CONFIDENTIAL NURSE & CLINICAL CORNER | STALL 5: HEADSPACE MELTON COMMUNITY HUB | STALL 6: MULTI-LINGUAL FAMILY & CALD LOUNGE |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Voluntary Cessation Plans & Self-Referral Bookings | Youth Mental Health & External Care Pathways | Bilingual Flyers & CALD Liaison Engagement |

**![][image24]**

**Key Elements of the Culminating Festival:**

1. **Student Ownership:** Year 9–10 Wellbeing Champions design, set up, and facilitate all six stalls, serving as visible peer role models (Bandura, 1977).  
     
2. **Confidential Help-Seeking:** The Secondary School Nurse and Headspace Melton representatives occupy dedicated, non-stigmatising hubs where students can ask questions or sign up for individual cessation plans without fear of disciplinary consequence (Thomas et al., 2025).  
     
3. **Cultural Safety & Inclusion:** All signage and informational handouts feature bilingual translations co-developed with Aurevian's CALD Liaison Officer, ensuring accessibility for East African, South Sudanese, and South Asian families.

**\[SECTION 1: CURRICULUM ARCHITECTURE & RATIONALE\]**  
**Integrated Curriculum Framework**  
Whole-school health promotion achieves maximum efficacy and sustainability when directly embedded within mandated curriculum structures rather than delivered as isolated, extra-curricular add-ons (Victorian Curriculum and Assessment Authority \[VCAA\], 2024; World Health Organisation \[WHO\], 2021).

**Project Unclouded** utilises a multi-disciplinary curriculum mapping matrix designed specifically for Victorian secondary schools. Aligned with the Victorian Curriculum F–10, the project integrates core learning areas to ensure rigorous academic standards while fostering student agency, health literacy, and critical thinking (VCAA, 2024):

1. **Health and Physical Education (HPE) — Levels 7 & 8:** Universal foundation focusing on analysing commercial determinants of health, norm correction, and social refusal assertiveness (Gardner et al., 2025).  
     
2. **Personal and Social Capability — Levels 9 & 10:** Targeted leadership domain empowering Year 9–10 Wellbeing Champions to collaborate, lead peer health initiatives, and build emotional self-regulation (Department of Education, 2021; Hunter, 2023).  
     
3. **Media Arts / English — Levels 9 & 10:** Cross-curricular application where students deconstruct commercial marketing tactics and co-design persuasive, multilingual health campaigns (Asdigian et al., 2023).
